metadata.title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
metadata.venue: ICSE '26 (48th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Software Engineering), Research Track, pp. 2938-2950, ACM
metadata.abstract_summary: A small domain-specific language (trigger / predicate / enforce) paired with a runtime that intercepts an LLM agent's next action before it executes, checks it against operator-authored or LLM-authored rules, and applies one of four enforcement strategies — evaluated, with the identical mechanism, against a code-execution agent, an embodied robot agent, and an Apollo-based autonomous-vehicle plann

sections.heading: Claims
sections.text: LLM agents deployed across code execution, embodied robotics, and autonomous driving share the same underlying risk shape — an autonomous decision-maker whose next action may violate a safety, legal, or operational constraint — but existing defenses were domain-specific (static analysis for code, motion constraints for robots, traffic rules for AVs) or too coarse (blocking whole tool classes rather than specific unsafe invocations). AgentSpec's claim is that a single lightweight rule language, interposed as a runtime monitor between an agent's decision and its actuator/tool call, can express and enforce constraints across all three domains at once, catching unsafe *specific* actions rather than over-blocking safe ones, at negligible runtime overhead.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text:
- **Language:** an ANTLR4-generated grammar (`AgentSpec.g4`) compiling rules of the shape `trigger <event> / check <predicate> / enforce <strategy>`. Predicates are Python functions taking the user's original request, the concrete tool/action input, and prior intermediate steps.
- **Runtime:** an interpreter (`interpreter.py`/`enforcement.py`) wraps a LangChain agent and intercepts each proposed tool call before dispatch, applying one of four enforcement strategies: `stop` (halt before execution), `user_inspection` (pause for human approval), `invoke_action` (substitute a pre-registered safe alternative), or `llm_self_examine` (return the violation to the model and ask it to revise its own plan while still pursuing the original request).
- **Rule authorship, both manual and generated:** hand-written rules (`src/rules/manual/`) cover roughly 30 real tool APIs (Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Binance, Venmo, Twilio, and others); a second set (`src/rules/llm/`) is GPT-4o/o1-generated and separately evaluated for quality against the hand-written set.
- **Three evaluation domains:** RedCode-Exec (750 code-execution test cases across 25 vulnerability types) and ToolEmu for code agents; SafeAgentBench (250 embodied-agent tasks across 11 categories, 10 unsafe/1 safe) for robot agents; and 8 FixDrive law-violation scenarios run against an Apollo/uDrive-instrumented autonomous-vehicle stack, with AgentSpec rules translated into uDrive runtime-plan adjustments by a dedicated translator (`src/spec_lang/translator`).

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Reported results: prevents unsafe executions in over 90% of code-agent test cases, eliminates all hazardous actions in the embodied-agent benchmark, and enforces 100% compliance in the autonomous-vehicle scenarios, with enforcement overhead in the low milliseconds.
- **Authors' own stated limitations (Section 6.3, Threats to Validity):** enforcement is deterministic and checkpoint-based — the system "does not reason about the long-term consequences of current actions," i.e. it has no trajectory-level foresight and cannot anticipate an unsafe state several steps ahead of the triggering action. Evaluations requiring manual judgment (assessing `user_inspection` outcomes) carry human-evaluation risk, mitigated by cross-validation, predefined criteria, and blind evaluation rather than eliminated. Rules risk overfitting to the evaluation set during development, mitigated by a 1:9 test/demonstration split rather than held-out validation against unrelated rules. The paper itself notes it does not run direct empirical baseline comparisons against competing runtime-enforcement systems (NeMo Guardrails, GuardAgent, and syntactic-enforcement approaches are discussed qualitatively in §6.1, not benchmarked head-to-head) — the reported percentages are enforcement-on vs. enforcement-off, not AgentSpec vs. alternative.
- Stated future work: probabilistic, foresight-based enforcement using Discrete-Time Markov Chain modeling to anticipate unsafe states proactively rather than only reacting at the triggering checkpoint.
